citations.narrative:
The facility has been conducting regulated activity without a valid USDA license. The facility’s Class C exhibitor license
was canceled by the licensee on March 12, 2024. Despite the cancellation, the facility continued to exhibit animals to the
public for compensation.
On April 25, 2026, the exhibitor attended the Keep Athens-Limestone Beautiful, Inc. (KALB) Annual Earth Day Expo in
Athens, Alabama where he provided animal entertainment services. Photographs posted on the Keep Athens-Limestone
Beautiful social media page show two black-handed spider monkeys on leashes being used for hands on public
encounters. Adults and children were observed holding, petting, and interacting directly with the animals.
On June 9th, 2026, the inspector spoke with the KALB Director who stated that she paid $935.00 for the animal encounter
and booked the animal entertainment through an online vendor platform, GigSalad. She selected the exhibitor listed as
“Wild Encounters,” whose profile indicated that he was a USDA licensed exhibitor with 25 years of animal experience and
has 27 reviews from other events he had attended with his animals. She confirmed that the images from the social media
page was of their event, provided receipts and confirmation number of the transaction with the exhibitor, and that this
exhibitor came to the event with the two black-handed spider monkeys.
Conducting regulated activity without a USDA license does not comply with the Animal Welfare Act or ensure that APHIS
officials can assess the care of the animals. Continuing to conduct regulated activity without a license is a serious
violation of the Animal Welfare Act. No regulated activities may be conducted until a USDA license is obtained.
This inspection was conducted with an IES investigator and a facility representative and the exit interview was conducted
with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
RICHARD HARGIS, Investigator n
